firstUse.quote: And was thilk ſame ſong of Colins owne making? / Ah fooliſh boy, that is with loue yblent:
firstUse.source: 1579, Immeritô [pseudonym; Edmund Spenser], “Aprill. Ægloga Quarta.”, in The Shepheardes Calender: […], London: […] Hugh Singleton, […], folio 14, recto:

ybound.hook: Wiktionary gives no earlier form for this sense.

firstUse.quote: Took he there, this gentle Knight, With men of armès strong, And led him home to Nottingham ward Ybound both hand and foot.
